intro.title: What is RAG? An AI knowledge base, in plain words
intro.subtitle: RAG stands for retrieval augmented generation: answers generated from a search across your documents. In practice, it is a chatbot built on your company's documents that does not answer from memory but by looking up your files.

ask.title: Ask the way you would ask a colleague
ask.desc: “How many vacation days do I get?” or “What does the contract with this supplier say about penalties?”. No more digging folder by folder.

search.title: The AI searches your documents, not the internet
search.desc: It only looks at the documents your company chooses to load, so answers follow your policies instead of some random web page.

cite.title: It answers and shows you where it came from
cite.desc: Every answer includes the citation from the document so you can check it. If the information is not in your documents, it tells you.

intro.analogy: Think of it as a new employee who has read every company manual and, every time they answer, shows you the paragraph they took it from.

sectors.title: Use cases by industry
sectors.subtitle: A chatbot built on your company's documents helps wherever people waste time looking for information in manuals, contracts or regulations.

how.title: How retrieval augmented generation (RAG) works
how.subtitle: Four steps between your documents and a cited answer.
how.diagramLabel: Diagram: documents, index, search and cited answer

docs.title: Documents
docs.desc: We extract the text from your PDF, Word, TXT files or web pages and split it into paragraph-based chunks. Each chunk remembers which document it came from.

index.title: Index
index.desc: Chunks are stored in a search index on the server. The AI model is not retrained: your documents live in the index, not inside the model.

search.title: Search
search.desc: For each question, the system retrieves the most relevant chunks (the “retrieval”). In the demo, search is lexical, BM25-style, and keeps the top 5.

answer.title: Cited answer
answer.desc: A language model (GPT-4o mini from OpenAI by default) writes the answer from those chunks and tags each fact with [1], [2]… so you can open the source.

example.title: Illustrative example
example.question: How far in advance do I need to request vacation?
example.answer: You must request it in writing from your direct manager at least 15 business days in advance [1].
example.sourceQuote: “Vacation must be requested in writing from the direct manager at least 15 business days in advance…”

security.title: Security and privacy of your documents
security.subtitle: This is what the system does today with your documents and your questions.

storage.title: Where your documents are stored
storage.desc: On KopTup's server. That is where we extract the text, split it into chunks and build the search index. Questions and answers are also logged on that server.

provider.title: Which AI provider we use
provider.desc: OpenAI, through its API. The default model is GPT-4o mini. The OpenAI access key stays on our server: it never reaches the browser.

sent.title: What is sent to OpenAI
sent.desc: Only what is needed to write each answer: your question, the most relevant chunks (not the whole document), the assistant's instructions and the latest messages of the conversation.

training.title: Your documents do not train the AI
training.desc: Under OpenAI's current API policy, data sent through the API is not used to train its models by default. OpenAI may keep it for up to 30 days to detect abuse.

control.title: If you need more control
control.desc: The Professional plan adds role-based permissions, and the Enterprise plan is deployed in your cloud or on your own servers (on-premise), with SSO and audit logs.

demo.title: In the public demo
demo.desc: The demo is for trying out how it works: do not upload confidential information.

accuracy.title: How we avoid made-up answers
accuracy.subtitle: An AI that makes up answers is worse than no AI at all. That is why the system follows three rules.

onlyDocs.title: It only answers with what is in your documents
onlyDocs.desc: The model receives the chunks found in your documents and the instruction to rely on them, not on what it “knows” from the internet.

cites.title: It cites the source
cites.desc: Every answer shows which document and chunk it comes from, so you can check it before using it.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions about RAG systems

whatIsRag.a: RAG (retrieval augmented generation) is a technique that combines a search engine with a language model: it first finds the chunks of your documents that answer the question, and then the AI writes the answer with that information, citing the source. It works like an AI knowledge base you can ask in natural language.

vsChatgpt.q: How is it different from ChatGPT?
vsChatgpt.a: ChatGPT answers with what it learned during training and does not know your company's internal documents. A RAG system first searches your documents, answers with what it finds there and shows you the source; plus, you decide which documents it uses. To write the answers we use OpenAI models, from the company behind ChatGPT, through its API.

training.q: Are my documents used to train the AI?
training.a: No. We do not train any model with your documents: the system looks them up for each question and only sends OpenAI the question, the relevant chunks and the latest messages of the conversation. Under OpenAI's current API policy, data sent through the API is not used to train its models by default; OpenAI may keep it for up to 30 days to detect abuse, or longer if the law requires it.

notFound.q: What happens if the answer is not in my documents?
notFound.a: The assistant tells you “I couldn't find that information” instead of making up an answer. Those questions help you spot which documents are missing: once you load them, the assistant can answer.

formats.a: PDF with text, Word (DOCX), TXT and web pages. Depending on the plan, we can also connect documents from Google Drive or SharePoint and data from databases or APIs. If your PDFs are scans (images without text), we review it with you during the pilot.

whatsapp.a: Yes. From the Professional plan, the assistant answers on your website and on WhatsApp, through the official WhatsApp Business API. Meta's WhatsApp message fees are billed separately, at cost.

cost.a: The {pilotWeeks}-week pilot costs {pilotPrice}. The Essential plan costs {essentialSetup} for setup plus {essentialMonthly} per month; Professional, {proSetup} for setup plus {proMonthly} per month; and Enterprise starts at {enterpriseSetup}, with a monthly fee based on the SLA. All prices are plus VAT where applicable.

time.a: The pilot with your documents takes {pilotWeeks} weeks. Implementation takes {essentialWeeks} weeks on the Essential plan, {proWeeks} weeks on Professional and {enterpriseWeeks} weeks on Enterprise.
